variants.prompt: Build a Vue 3 counter component with increment/decrement and a zero floor. Use reactive state and guard the decrement so it never goes negative. Call out disabled states and clean template logic. Concepts: vue, components, reactivity, event handlers, basics. Framework focus: Vue SFC patterns, ref/reactive state, computed/watch, and v-model bindings.

constraints: Start at 0 and display the current value.
Support increment, decrement, and reset.
Never allow a negative value.
Disable decrement while the value is 0.
publicRequirements.prompt: Start with a reliable counter. Keep the behavior small, explicit, and state-driven.
publicRequirements.title: Base correctness

constraints: Add a labeled step selector with 1, 5, and 10.
Use 1 as the default step.
Apply the selected step to both increment and decrement.
Clamp decrement at 0 when the selected step is larger than the value.
publicRequirements.prompt: The product team now needs larger jumps without duplicating counter logic.
publicRequirements.title: Configurable step

variants.prompt: Build a small Todo List in Vue 3 using the Composition API and <script setup>. Users should be able to add tasks, mark them as completed, remove individual tasks, and clear all completed tasks. Framework focus: Vue SFC patterns, ref/reactive state, computed/watch, and v-model bindings.

constraints: Trim task text and reject empty or whitespace-only submissions.
Disable Add while the normalized input is empty.
Support both form submission with Enter and the Add button.
Clear the input after a successful add and assign every task a stable unique id.
publicRequirements.prompt: Start with reliable task creation. Treat input normalization and identity as part of the state contract.
publicRequirements.title: Core transitions

constraints: Provide All, Active, and Completed filters that derive the visible rows from the source list.
Expose the selected filter with aria-pressed.
Announce the remaining active-task count with correct singular and plural copy.
Clear completed tasks without removing active tasks.
publicRequirements.prompt: The list now needs trustworthy derived views. Filtering must never discard or rewrite source tasks.
publicRequirements.title: Derived filters

variants.title: Todo List (Refs + List Rendering)

variants.prompt: Build a simple paginated data table in Vue 3 that shows a static list of users. Display 5 rows per page, with Previous / Next controls and a "Page X of Y" indicator. Disable the navigation buttons appropriately on the first and last pages. Vue focus: keep page index in a ref and derive page slices with computed. Framework focus: Vue SFC patterns, ref/reactive state, computed/watch, and v-model bindings.

constraints: Render 13 users in stable source order with a default page size of five.
Previous and Next must move one page at a time without leaving the valid page range.
The final page must render only users 11 through 13 and disable Next.
Keep the existing footer button order and page-info contract intact.
publicRequirements.prompt: Start with pagination users can trust. Every page must expose the correct slice and guard both boundaries.
publicRequirements.title: Core page window

constraints: Trim the query and match name, email, or role case-insensitively.
Every query change must reset pagination to page one.
Derive page counts from the filtered collection and keep the page range valid.
Render a single empty-state row and disable both pagination controls when nothing matches.
publicRequirements.prompt: Now layer search onto pagination. Normalization, result counts, empty state, and the active page must stay synchronized.
publicRequirements.title: Filter and page reset

constraints: Sort ID numerically and Name or Role case-insensitively.
The first activation of a new column must sort ascending and the second descending.
Equal sort values must retain their original source order.
Changing sort or page size must reset to page one and recompute the page window.
publicRequirements.prompt: Add deterministic sorting and a second page size without letting derived state drift or compare numeric ids as strings.
publicRequirements.title: Sort and page size

variants.title: Vue Paginated Data Table

variants.prompt: Build a small shopping cart UI in Vue 3. Show a list of products, let the user add them to the cart, adjust quantities, remove items, and display derived totals for item count and price. Vue focus: use reactive arrays and computed totals. Framework focus: Vue SFC patterns, ref/reactive state, computed/watch, and v-model bindings.

constraints: Add a new product as one cart row with quantity 1.
Adding the same product again must increment its existing row instead of creating a duplicate.
Keep different products in separate rows with their own quantities and line totals.
Derive total item count, line totals, and the overall total from the current cart. Format every amount as USD with two decimal places.
publicRequirements.prompt: Start with a trustworthy cart model. Product identity, quantities, and money must stay consistent as items are added.
publicRequirements.title: Core cart transitions

constraints: Increasing and decreasing a quantity must update its row total, total item count, and overall total.
Decreasing an item at quantity 1 must remove that row.
Remove must delete only the selected product and leave every other row unchanged.
An empty cart must report 0 items and a $0.00 total.
publicRequirements.prompt: Now make every quantity transition safe. Updates must affect only their target row and return cleanly to an empty cart.
publicRequirements.title: Quantity boundaries

constraints: Use stock limits of 2 Wireless Headphones, 3 Mechanical Keyboards, 5 Ergonomic Mice, and 1 USB-C Hub.
Show the remaining product stock contract as 2 in stock, 3 in stock, 5 in stock, and 1 in stock before cart changes.
Disable both Add to cart and Increase when a cart line reaches its product's stock limit, and never allow either path to exceed stock.
Re-enable Add to cart and Increase after the quantity drops below the limit.
Announce `Wireless Headphones reached its stock limit.` through a stable atomic polite cart status when that limit is reached.
publicRequirements.prompt: Inventory is finite. Preserve the cart guarantees while every add path respects stock and communicates the boundary.
publicRequirements.title: Inventory guard

variants.prompt: Build a Material-like invite field in Vue 3. As users type, show autocomplete suggestions, convert selections into removable chips, and support keyboard shortcuts (Enter/comma/backspace).

constraints: Filter candidates by name or email with trimmed, case-insensitive matching and show at most six suggestions.
Selecting a suggestion by click must add exactly one chip, clear the query, and close the listbox.
Exclude selected candidates from later suggestions without mutating the source candidate list.
Use stable candidate ids so suggestion and chip identity does not depend on the rendered index.
publicRequirements.prompt: Start with a trustworthy autocomplete contract. Filtering and selection must stay predictable across casing, pointer input, and repeated queries.
publicRequirements.title: Core suggestion selection

constraints: Enter and comma must add a trimmed custom chip and clear the input.
Whitespace-only input must add nothing and return the input to an empty value.
Reject duplicates by candidate id or case-insensitive normalized value.
A remove control must delete only its target chip and expose the target label in its accessible name.
publicRequirements.prompt: Now make free-form entry safe. Token boundaries, duplicate identity, and targeted removal must behave the same for every input path.
publicRequirements.title: Token normalization

constraints: ArrowUp and ArrowDown must wrap through the visible suggestions and update a stable active-descendant id.
Enter must select the active option while keeping focus on the input.
Escape must close the listbox and clear the active option without deleting the query or chips.
Backspace on an empty input must remove only the final chip.
publicRequirements.prompt: Complete the combobox keyboard lifecycle. The active option, open state, chip selection, and destructive shortcuts must never drift apart.
publicRequirements.title: Keyboard lifecycle

constraints: Allow at most five chips, disable the input at the limit, and guard programmatic or keyboard add paths from exceeding it.
Removing a chip below the limit must immediately re-enable entry and allow another invite.
Put the combobox role and relationships on the actual input; use a labelled listbox, stable option ids, and product-specific remove labels.
Keep an always-rendered polite, atomic status region and remove document listeners when the preview unmounts.
publicRequirements.prompt: Finish with a hard invite boundary and a complete assistive-technology contract. Limits must be enforced through every event path and announced without unstable DOM regions.
publicRequirements.title: Invite limit and accessibility

variants.prompt: Implement a Vue 3 debounced search input that calls a fake API. Use a watcher with a timeout, cancel stale calls, and manage loading/error/empty states. This mirrors real-world search UX. Concepts: vue, composition-api, watch. Vue focus: debounce with watch + timeout cleanup and reactive loading state. Framework focus: Vue SFC patterns, ref/reactive state, computed/watch, and v-model bindings.

constraints: Treat the trimmed input as the search query.
Restart the 500 ms debounce window whenever the query changes.
Do not show results before the final query finishes its debounce and request.
Render matching users with the existing result-row contract.
publicRequirements.prompt: Start with a dependable search flow that waits for the final query before showing results.
publicRequirements.title: Base debounce

constraints: Show the fake API failure for the query error without leaving loading active.
Show an explicit no-results state for a completed search with no matches.
Clear stale errors and results when a new query starts.
Treat whitespace-only input as empty and return to the initial prompt.
publicRequirements.prompt: The interviewer now wants every terminal state to recover cleanly when the user keeps typing.
publicRequirements.title: State recovery

constraints: Clear old result rows as soon as a newer non-empty query starts.
Cancel or ignore every response that no longer belongs to the current query.
A stale response must not change results, loading, or error state.
Keep loading active until the current request settles.
publicRequirements.prompt: Assume requests can overlap. Only the newest query may commit results or finish the loading state.
publicRequirements.title: Latest query wins

constraints: Connect the input to stable search-status and search-results regions with aria-describedby and aria-controls.
Expose the status row as an atomic polite live region.
Expose request activity with aria-busy and errors with role alert.
Cancel both a pending debounce and an already-started fake request during teardown.
Do not update state after the component unmounts or is destroyed.
publicRequirements.prompt: Finish by making state announcements explicit and proving that teardown leaves no search timer behind.
publicRequirements.title: Accessible lifecycle
